subject: Conference follow-up: inference needs / discovery recap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@edgefintech.io>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Conference follow-up: inference needs / discovery recap

Hi Lisa — it was great meeting you at the AI Summit last week. Thanks again for taking 30 minutes to walk through EdgeFintech's fraud-detection pipeline and where you see model inference fitting in. Per our call, I wanted to summarize next steps and confirm availability for a technical deep-dive with our serving team.

Recap (high-level):
- Current: on-premise LLM ensemble (2 models) + custom pre/post processing. Throughput needs: ~120 QPS peak; latency SLO: 95th < 220ms.
- Main pain: unpredictable tail latency during peak batch jobs, and high per-token cost after tokenization/overhead.
- Desired: predictable latency, lower unit cost, and a rollout path for mixed private/hosted deployment.

Proposed next steps:
1) 30-45 minute technical deep-dive (Marissa + Camila + our serving eng): scope batching, KV caching, and quantization tradeoffs.
2) Share a short one-pager and discovery notes (attached).
3) If aligned, run a small RPS/latency POC on a dedicated pool.

Availability: Camila and I are free Mon/Tue next week (May 17-18) 10:00-12:00 PT or 14:00-16:00 PT. If those don't work, please send 2-3 times that work for you.

Attachments: Redwood-OnePager.pdf; Discovery-Notes-20270512.docx

Thanks — looking forward to continuing the conversation.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive

If timing changed or someone else on your team is owning this, could you point me to the right person or let me know a better time to follow up?

If now isn't a priority, no problem — I'll check back in a few weeks.
